name: figma-nested-frames-quiz-board
story: A designer built a quiz board out of nested auto-layout frames, renamed only the rows that mattered to them (Question, Answer A-D), and exported the page frame as SVG with ids on.
idioms: four and five levels of <g id="Frame NNNNNNNNNN"> wrappers with Figma's big numeric default names (Frame 1000004321, Frame 427320567, Frame 1707478242, Frame 21)
auto-layout backing shapes keep their default names too (id="Rectangle 118".."Rectangle 122")
a Figma text layer is named after its own content until renamed, so id="Amsterdam" on the <text> that reads Amsterdam is a DEFAULT name, not an authored label
the meaningful layer names sit only on the leaf group wrappers, one level (A/B/C) or two (D, via Frame 21) above the text
the whole tree inside <g clip-path="url(#clip0_58_1102)"> with the matching <defs><clipPath>
no <?xml?> prolog, zero indentation, fill="none" on the root, uppercase hex, fill-opacity for layer alpha
whyThisMatters: Auto-layout is how Figma boards are actually built, so labels have to come from the nearest MEANINGFUL name: an importer that takes the text node's own id gives the operator five fields called Amsterdam, Helsinki, Melbourne, Reykjavik and the full question string, and one that walks up to the nearest named ancestor without discounting Figma's defaults gives five fields called Frame 21 and Frame 1000004322.
